earlier_root.description: The develop root (before this change): its health reports no guest contract or payload revision, its storage.sh imports the owned pool only with `zpool import -N -d $vdev $guid` and refuses otherwise.

forced_stop.method: Daemon death, the only way besides the readiness timeout to end an upgrade before commit (design: the upgrade owns the mutation gate and refuses a forced stop). A watcher polled serial.log every 0.1 s after the pre-upgrade line count and sent SIGKILL to the runtime service process (pid 84754) on the first `MACUS_OBSERVATION v1 stage=incus` after `MACUS_OBSERVATION v1 stage=storage`, and only while upgrade.pending existed. The storage service had then finished (`Preparing persistent Incus data and configured shares ... [ ok ]`), so the new root had adopted and imported the pool, and incusd was starting on it. The Virtualization.framework VM process ended with the daemon, without a guest shutdown or pool export.
forced_stop.first_attempt: The first watcher keyed on `TAMA_STORAGE_ZFS_READY`, which the guest prints only in a log dump after `TAMA_BOOTSTRAP_READY`; it appeared 5 s after the upgrade committed, the watcher saw no upgrade.pending and did not kill. That upgrade (backup 20261125T123120Z-c9145d09) committed in 48 s with the inventory compared, and `runtime upgrade --rollback` restored the develop root in 6 s (root-only, data kept; replaced state kept as 20261125T123246Z-4ee102df). The develop root then started ready in 38 s on the same inodes as before, and the second attempt ran from there.
